title: Combination Sum III
summary: Find all unique combinations of k numbers between 1 and 9 that sum up to n, ensuring no number is repeated.
statement: Find all unique combinations of k numbers between 1 and 9 that sum up to n, ensuring no number is repeated. Return a list of all valid combinations without duplicates, in any order.
constraints: Choose exactly k DISTINCT numbers from 1 through 9 whose sum is n. Return each combination once; combinations and the numbers within them may appear in any order.
target_time_complexity: O(2^9 × 9), bounded by the nine available digits
hints: Both the digit count and the sum must match, and no digit can be reused.
Choose digits in increasing order so each combination is constructed once.
Recursively choose the next digit above the previous one, reduce the remaining count and sum, and record only when both reach zero.
Prune when the remaining sum is below the smallest possible distinct-digit total or above the largest one.
editorial: Increasing choices eliminate permutations of the same combination and prevent digit reuse. The recursion tracks the next allowed digit, remaining slots, and remaining sum. Minimum/maximum possible sums prune impossible branches. The independent oracle enumerates all 512 subsets of digits 1–9 and filters by size and sum. Although the input domain is finite, its 480 (k,n) pairs easily support distinct visible/hidden cases; a regression exhausts every pair, in addition to the 500 seeded comparisons.

tests.explanation: The only three distinct digits summing to 7 are 1,2,4. Repeating a digit or using fewer than three does not qualify.
The three valid combinations are [1,2,6], [1,3,5], and [2,3,4]; each contains exactly three different digits.
